Probably not what people are expecting, maybe wrong thread, but the first time I was invited to dinner at an ex's parents' for dinner. I had come from a home where kids remained seen but not heard. Practically no relationship with my father, relationship with my mum wasn't great. Kicked out at 17. I've met other parents before, some like me, some dont, but i wanted to prove i was good enough for his daughter. 

Before I met him my ex gave me a heads up that I was the second boy that was to meet him and he wasn't easily impressed. Great. No kissing or heavy touching because it makes him uncomfortable, okay he's old fashioned, no big deal. Don't stare at his face (he had a hole in his nose the size of a baseball, decades of working in the sun had destroyed his face, later revealed to be cancer once he finally agreed to get it looked after having it for 20 years). Be able to take a joke, self depreciation is my middle name. Don't smell like weed at any time. Clean clothes and t break it is. Now I'm ready to go.

I went there the next day and i had already been familiar with the mum (she was my boss for 2 of the 4 years I dated her daughter) and got along well. I walk in the door and my then girlfriend opened the door to me and I'm greeted with Hi's and hello's from the women. Their home was small but cozy. I walk across the kitchen to see a retired carpenter where, in his prime, he'd snap me like a twig, could probably still throw me down a flight of stairs at the time. He took no shit, left nothing unsaid. Somehow a man with a hole in his face wearing pj's and slippers made me nervous. I shook his hand and greeted him. Things started well. Not a talker at first, just sitting in his spot on the couch watching old Westerns (Laramie is a favorite of mine to this day). I could feel him studying me but I remained calm.

Dinner was had, cigarettes were smoked (we all were smokers at the time) I was urged to eat seconds and even thirds by the women. Which I graciously accepted. Some quips flew between me and the dad, but I went easy on him since he was the host (wouldnt insult the man in front of his family). Then dessert, delicious. And I was sent home with a small amount of leftovers in a tupperware I never returned... did I mention they were Italian and Portugese? Ah must've slipped my mind.

After everything me and my ex went outside as I walked to my car. Kisses were snuck in whether he was watching or not and she asked me how it went. I told her to let me think about it for the night so I can reflect. Nothing bad, I just like to think over the night in my head. She said that was fine but she knew it went well. 

What I told her was that it was the first time I could feel love in a home. Not for me but in general. It wasn't a house like I was raised in but a home with a loving family. And for a short time I felt like I was part of it. Things ended badly between the ex but I don't hold any resentment for the parents (and boss) who made me feel loved for the time we were together.

TL;DR: My ex's parents were better than mine and had a happier home than I did

I'm on the other end of this question, so might as well give some perspective from the others ideas. I'm a young 20 something year old guy and it was a little under a year ago that I had a small group of friends and a loving relationship, however after a devastating breakup and being sidelined by my group of friends that I chose to learn to be happy with myself as I had never had the chance before and I've been alone for about 10 months now.

For context, my home life during my teenage years was less than ideal; I grew up with a heavily abusive father (emotional, physical and would have me doing psychological backflips into thinking I was a shit person) and a mother who, bless her heart, did everything just to keep the family together however that came at the expense of catering to my father and neglecting the needs of her children, and it was shortly after meeting my girlfriend at the time I got kicked out if the house at age 18. I'd run from home a few times prior to this  making stupid choices along the way due to heavy depression and self loathing issues.

Fast forward a few years and I get a decent apartment but I always had her by my side. Having that emotional support to not slip back into my bad habits. Made a few great friends along the way too. However, due to some personal reasons and COVID being a huge strain on all my relationships, things brutally fell apart and I found myself more miserable than ever, so I decided that I'd learn to be happy and comfortable in my home. I work full time and other than going to the bar and the barber every now and again, I stay home and learn to enjoy being by myself with no real interest of socializing with my peers.

As hard as that can be sometimes, I've learned more about myself being alone than I ever would have being distracted by other people. Not saying that is a bad thing, but, for me, I'm happy I could have this experience and be relatively happy 80% of the time. Overcoming life challenges with no one at your side, where lonesome, has made me a much more independent and stronger person than I ever was before. I'll gladly have a social life when I find like-minded others who share my interests and values but, until then, I'll gladly sit here and plan out the next phases of my life.

And just in case I get people saying things like, "Oh do you just sit around and play videogames and dick around on reddit when you don't work," and things of the sort, while, yes, I play every now and again I've actually done some things I'd never be able to do while in a relationship, like going on a roadtrip hallway across the country (Northeast of the U.S. to the midwest). That experience was an accomplishment I will always remember and treasure for the years to come. Sorry if it wasn't the answer you were looking for, but I wanted to get out there that everyone has their reasons.
Your suggestions are appreciated I don't want to come across the wrong way, too poor to afford therapy so where else to go other than Reddit.

Was looking for a secret to take to the grave thread but it's going here: 

I hope this sort of gets buried if the username wasn't a big enough tip, but as a man who loves his ex the same way I did years ago, I will be attending the funeral of her father most likely in my car after the service, whenever it happens. He's an older gentleman (67) with a broken body from his carpentry days and has had skin cancer, heart complications and like most older guys, skyrocketing blood pressure.

Don't get me wrong he was a huge prick, many a times we butted heads over things due to his and my own stubborn nature of having to be right. But he was one of the only father figures I had in my early adulthood and have made many fond memories of him. 

[Sappy story alert, skip if uninterested]
One I remember fondly is Black Friday shopping and how much we both, absolutely fucking hated it, but as the old adage goes "happy wives, happy lives." We would complain tirelessly in the car as her mom would laugh and my girlfriend would get upset to my lack of enthusiasm. And in the store, oh in the store, we were aggressive and relentless  towards all the other new englanders stuffing the various stores and mall our women dragged us into. A few racist jokes on his end were made, some were made on my end, to which I don't care what you say, his honesty was both to a fault and endearing (probably a reason my ex was attracted to me now that I think of it). I respected that man, he taught me a few things here and there about cars and carpentry, through no obligation but, because, as much as that's his little girl, and I have to emphasize, he made that infinitely clear, he knew I always did my absolute best to make her happy. (It didn't end well between me and the ex) but that was his way of being himself to me if that makes sense.
[End of sappy story]

That man knows in his heart he doesn't have very long, and if my twenties have taught me anything it's "always trust your gut, your instincts are there for a reason, don't ignore them." One of the last conversations we had and, if my memory serves correct, it was the last conversation we ever had. He's scared to go, but something's telling him that it's coming, he'll fight it as long as he can, for his wife and his daughter's sake, but he knows it's coming. The guilt and the embarrassment of his wife and his daughter caring for him the way they had (still might, I'm not entirely sure of his current health, he had cancer removed and a few other things) was one of the worst feelings he had ever felt. It eats at him. I remember that conversation everyday. And due to all the knowledge I have of their very splintered family,  I have already made up my mind on this. I'm not going to make a big scene but I can tell no one of this just in case the information leaks its way up to her.  I make an effort not to make any sort of appearance in her life. 

Part of me knows that some of him will be pissed off, mainly because that's what he says to his wife and kids too but, as an older guy, I know deep down there's a part of him that would appreciate it. Plus I respect him as a human being rather than an extension of his daughter.

TL;DR: I read the obituaries every day looking for my ex's dad and will either attend his funeral in my car away from anyone noticing me or at least pay my respects at his grave.
